headline.answer: Edit the "headline" value ("FUEL WELL. LIVE WELL.") under sections.header in nutrition/fixture.json. source/nutrition.mjs renders it as #header_headline in Barlow Condensed Bold (66px) and auto-shrinks it if wider than 830px. For a quick test without editing JSON, A also shows an inline CLI override (--set sections.header.headline="..."), though whether that printed command runs cannot be verified from the image.

artwork.answer: Two pictured routes: (1) fastest swap: replace nutrition/assets/web/leaf_glow.png with a new transparent PNG (~2:3 portrait; must stay PNG because default Satori/Resvg drops WebP), or (2) add a new ID: register it in PNG_IDS inside source/nutrition.mjs and update hero.illustrationId (currently "leaf_glow") in nutrition/fixture.json.

Keep PNG format—default Satori/Resvg drops WebP."), right-hand "TRANSPARENT PNG" checkerboard preview labeled "leaf_glow.png · 427x640", and green arrow pointing to the green-outlined "2 #hero_img" leaf box on "FINISHED POSTER".

export.answer: After invocation via source/render.mjs (runCLI) with nutrition/fixture.json: (1) source/nutrition.mjs runs validate() to check the fixture schema and 1000x1000 budget, then buildScene() merges copy, the Barlow Condensed font, and pinned PNGs into a scene; (2) source/render.mjs (processRequest) calls renderSatori() to build an SVG plus the hero <feDropShadow> and iteratively shrink overflowing text (x0.9, max 10x); (3) @resvg/resvg-js rasterizes the fitted SVG into PNG bytes; (4) publishArtifacts() -> publishStaged() stages runs/<uuid>/render.png, result.json, and SHA-256 digests, then atomically swaps manifest.json to publish the poster. Cannot tell from the image alone whether the printed CLI command actually runs or how --out out/ (3A), runs/<uuid>/render.png (3D), and nutrition/render.png (poster header) reconcile.
export.location: Panel 3 ("3 ONE WORKING ROUTE TO THE EXPORTED PNG", full-width bottom band): top-right flow pill "SOURCE EDITS -> CLI -> SCENE -> FIT & RASTERIZE -> RENDER.PNG" and four arrow-linked cards left-to-right ("3A RUN ONE COMMAND", "3B VALIDATE & BUILD SCENE", "3C LAYOUT, FIT & RASTERIZE", "3D PUBLISH VERIFIED PNG"), connected downward from Panels 1-2 via "INPUTS" and upward to "FINISHED POSTER" via "WRITES PNG".

reason: Poster A wins for the newcomer task at native size because of three concrete visible aids that directly unblock the tasks rather than merely adding detail: (1) in Panel 2, the file pill (nutrition/assets/web/leaf_glow.png), transparent-checkerboard preview, PNG-only note, and PNG_IDS bullet tell a newcomer how to replace the leaf with new art, whereas B's "2 Swap the leaf" only shows switching to one existing ID (parfait_jar) and never locates the artwork file; (2) A's color-coded arrows and tight bounding boxes (#header_headline and #hero_img) plus JSON snippets unambiguously tie edits to poster regions, whereas B floats badge 1 on the preview's outer margin; and (3) A's cards 3B-3C explicitly trace layout-to-pixel causality (buildScene -> renderSatori SVG -> @resvg/resvg-js rasterization) with full relative paths, whereas B jumps from "Place text and art" to "Playwright: Screenshot the page" with no directories or intermediate page step. B clearly beats A on 400px thumbnail legibility, and A's dense micro-type and unresolved output-path tension (nutrition/render.png vs --out out/ vs runs/<uuid>/render.png) hinder quick scanning, but A actually answers all three newcomer questions.
